title: The Best U.S. States for Growing Your Savings Faster
description: A guide to 'Geo-Arbitrage' and the impact of SALT taxes.
content:
Where you live determines how fast you build wealth. A salary of $100,000 in New York City results in a radically different savings rate than $100,000 in Austin, Texas. The difference isn't just rent; it's taxes. High-tax states take up to 13% of your income off the top, while 0% income tax states let you keep it. Combined with Cost of Living (COL) differences, moving to a 'Wealth-Friendly' state can accelerate your retirement timeline by 5-10 years.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Sunshine Tax' vs. 'Freedom Dividend': Living in California costs you ~10% in income tax plus higher gas/sales tax. Moving to Tennessee saves that 10% instantly.
  • Property Tax Trap: Some 0% income tax states (Texas, New Hampshire) make up for it with massive Property Taxes (2%+). Renters win in these states; homeowners might break even.
  • The SALT Cap: The Federal 'State and Local Tax' deduction is capped at $10,000. High earners in high-tax states get double-taxed on everything above this cap. Moving solves this.
  • Remote Work Leverage: If you can keep a NYC salary while living in Florida, you unlock the ultimate wealth hack: High Income / Low Tax / Low Cost.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The 'Great Migration' of wealth from North/East to South/West is driven by tax policy. Florida and Texas have gained trillions in AGI (Adjusted Gross Income) from migrating professionals.

The State Tier List

Where can you save the most?

Tier 1: The Wealth Accelerators (0% Income Tax)

  • States: Florida, Texas, Tennessee, Nevada, Washington, Wyoming, South Dakota.
  • Pros: You keep ~5-10% more of your paycheck compared to average states.
  • Cons: Texas/Florida have high property taxes and insurance costs. Washington has high sales tax.
  • Verdict: Best for high W-2 earners and retirees withdrawing 401(k)s.

Tier 2: The Balanced Middle

  • States: North Carolina, Georgia, Arizona, Indiana.
  • Stats: Moderate flat tax (3-5%) but very low property tax and housing costs.
  • Verdict: Often cheaper overall than Tier 1 for homeowners because the property tax is so low.

Tier 3: The Wealth Drags

  • States: California, New York, New Jersey, Hawaii.
  • Stats: High Income Tax (up to 13%) + High Cost of Living.
  • Verdict: Only live here if your salary is 50% higher than what you could get elsewhere. You pay a premium for the location.

Running the Numbers

  1. The 'Paycheck' Simulation: Use a paycheck calculator (like SmartAsset). Compare a $100k salary in NY vs FL. The monthly difference is ~$400-$500. Invested over 20 years, that is $250,000 of lost wealth.
  2. The Housing Arbitrage: Sell a $800k condo in Boston. Buy a $400k house in Raleigh. Invest the $400k difference. You just funded your retirement.
  3. Retirement Tax: Some states don't tax Social Security or Pension income (e.g., Pennsylvania). Check state-specific retirement tax laws before settling down.
  4. Insurance Reality: Florida has 0% income tax but massive Home/Auto insurance costs. Ensure the tax savings aren't eaten by insurance premiums.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does remote work change my taxes?

Yes. You generally pay tax where you live/sleep, not where the company HQ is. If you move to Texas, you stop paying NY tax (usually). Check 'Convenience of the Employer' rules for NY.

Is it worth moving just for money?

No. Community and Family matter more. But if you are indifferent between two places, choose the one that makes you rich faster.

What about Sales Tax?

Tennessee has 0% income tax but ~9.5% sales tax. This hurts low spenders less than high spenders. If you are a saver (don't spend much), income tax matters more than sales tax.
